Milli Savunma Bakanı Yaşar Güler, TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonunda, Milli Savunma Bakanlığının 2027 yılı bütçe görüşmelerinin ardından milletvekillerinin sorularını yanıtladı.
Bakan Güler, dünyada ve bölgede yaşanan krizlerin, artan çatışmalar ve değişen tehdit ortamının, ülkeleri savunma harcamalarını artırmaya, askeri kabiliyetlerini geliştirmeye ve modernizasyon faaliyetlerini hızlandırmaya yönelttiğini anlattı.
Küresel ölçekte savunma harcamaları artmaya devam ederken, Türkiye'nin de savunma harcamaları çalışmalarını kararlılıkla sürdürdüğünü belirten Güler, "Özellikle İran'ın hedef ayrımı gözetmeyen saldırılarının da ortaya koyduğu üzere, hava ve füze tehditleriyle insansız hava araçlarının yaygınlaşması güçlü, çok katmanlı ve bütünleşik hava savunma sistemlerine duyulan ihtiyacı daha da artırmıştır." diye konuştu.
Güler, bahse konu gelişmeler karşısında Çelik Kubbe, milli muharip uçak, dronlar ve insansız sistemler gibi öncelikli projelerin hızlandırılmasına, hava savunma kabiliyetlerinin güçlendirilmesine, kritik tesis ve altyapıların korunmasına, mevcut sistemlerin modernizasyonuna, yeni nesil tehditlere karşı çok yönlü tedbirlerin geliştirilmesine öncelik verdiklerini vurguladı.
Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın iradesi ve destekleriyle 2026, 2027 ve 2028 yılları için hususi olarak bütçe tahsis edilmesinin önemine işaret eden Güler, hususi bütçe tahsisinin savunma sanayisinin seri üretim kapasitesinin artırılması ve ihtiyaç duyulan sistemlerin hızlıca envantere kazandırılması bakımından büyük önem taşıdığını söyledi.
Güler, savunma bütçesindeki artışın temel gerekçesinin, değişen güvenlik ortamının ortaya çıkardığı ihtiyaçlar doğrultusunda savunma sanayisinin üretim kapasitesini ve Türk Silahlı Kuvvetlerinin caydırıcılığını güçlendirerek, Türkiye'nin güvenliğini uzun vadede teminat altına almak olduğunu belirtti.
Bakanlık olarak şehitlerin emanetlerine sahip çıkmayı, gazilerin ve ailelerinin yanında durmayı, ihtiyaç ve taleplerini duyarlılıkla yaklaşmayı öncelikli görev gördüklerini dile getiren Güler, şunları kaydetti:
"Bu anlayışla gazilerimizin ve vazife malullerimizin sosyal ve özlük haklarını daha da geliştirmek, hayatın her alanda karşılaştıkları sorunlara çözüm üretmek ve ailelerimizin refahını artırmak için devletimizin imkanları ölçüsünde Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığımızın koordinesinde çalışmalarımızı sürdürüyoruz. Nitekim ağustos ayında Gazi Meclisimiz tarafından kabul edilen ilgili kanunla bu konuda önemli adımlar atılmıştır. 7594 sayılı kanunla erbaş ve er şehitlerimizin anne ve babalarına aylık bağlanmasında uygulanmakta olan asgari ücret alt sınırının tüm şehitlerin anne ve babalarına uygulanmasına bakıma muhtaç gazilere ödenen bakım yardımının asgari ücretin 2 katından 2,5 katına çıkarılmasına erbaş, er, gazi ve vazife malulleri için maluliyet derecesinin yeniden değerlendirilmesi talep etme yaşının 41'den 55'e çıkarılması sağlanmıştır. 3713 sayılı kanun kapsamındaki erbaş ve erler ile korucu ve sivillere bağlanacak aylıkların alt sınır ve göstergeler oranında artırılması, terörle mücadelede malul kalmayacak şekilde yaralananlardan derece belirlenenlere bağlanan aylıkların artırılması ve terörle mücadelede terörist silahıyla malul kalmayacak şekilde yaralananlara aylık bağlanması ve bazı haklar verilmesi imkanı da getirilmiştir."
Bakan Güler, 2027 Merkezi Yönetim Bütçe Kanunu teklifine göre, Şehit Yakını ve Gaziler Programı'nda tüm kamu idareleri için 30 milyar 25 milyon lira ödenek tahsisi de öngörüldüğünü ifade etti. Bahse konu ödeneğin koordinasyonundan Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığının sorumlu olduğunu belirten Güler, yönetiminin ise Cumhurbaşkanlığı Strateji ve Bütçe Başkanlığınca gerçekleştirileceğini söyledi.
Bakanlık bütçesine tahsis edilen ödeneklerin ise sadece ilama bağlı borçlar kapsamında yapılan ödemeler için olduğunu anlatan Güler, "Şehit yakınlarımıza ve gazilerimize yönelik hakların geliştirilmesinin yanı sıra, uzman erbaşlarımızın da özlük hakları ve kamu görevlerine geçiş imkanları dahil personelimizin geleceğine ilişkin iyileştirmeleri de yapıyoruz." dedi. Güler, bu kapsamda eğitim seviyesi uygun olanların 3. dereceden 1. dereceye yükselebilmelerinin sağlandığını belirtti.
"Bitirdikleri yüksek öğrenim süresine göre ilave kademeler ile 1 derece verilmesine imkan tanınmış uzman erbaşların astsubaylığa statü geçiş kontenjanları artırılmış, devlet memurları ile birlikte uzman erbaşların konutlardan faydalanma oranı yüzde 10'dan yüzde 20'ye çıkarılmıştır. Bunların yanı sıra emeklilik sürecine ilişkin olarak 55 yaşında yaş haddinden emeklilik hakkı getirilmiş, devlet memuru olarak istihdam edildikten sonra emekli olanların ise emekli aylıklarının doğrudan emekli olan uzman erbaşların emekli aylıklarıyla eşitlenmesi sağlanmıştır. Emeklileri dahil uzman erbaşlara 3600 ek göstergeden faydalanma hakkı verilmiştir."
Uzman çavuşların kamuya geçiş süreçlerinin mevcut mevzuat çerçevesinde yürütüldüğünü söyleyen Güler, sözleşmeli erbaş ve erler içinde de önemli iyileştirmeler yaptıklarını vurguladı. Bu kapsamda, görev şartlarının ağırlığı dikkate alınarak özel harekat ve operasyon tazminatından yararlanmalarının sağlandığını ve tutarın 63 bin lira seviyesine ulaştırıldığı aktaran Güler, "Sözleşme bitiminde ödenen tazminatlarda ise yüzde 33 oranında artış yapılmış böylece 7. hizmet yılını tamamlayarak ayrılan personele 2 milyon lira üzerinde ödeme gerçekleştirilmektedir. Bakanlığımız bünyesinde kalarak uzman erbaşlığa geçen sözleşmeli erbaş ve erlere de ikramiye imkanı getirilmiş. Uzman erbaşlığa geçiş için başvuru şartı 3 yıldan 2 yıla indirilmiştir." ifadelerini kullandı.
Bakan Güler, C-130 tipi askeri kargo uçağının kazasına ilişkin, "C-130 kazasına ilişkin analiz ve sonuçların değerlendirilmesine yönelik çalışmalarımız son aşamaya gelmiştir. Bu aşamada uçağın ana üreticisi Lockheed Martin tarafından incelenmesi talep edilen ilave parçalar gündeme gelmiştir. C-130 uçakları dünyanın birçok ülkesinde yaygın olarak kullanılmaya devam edilmektedir." bilgisini verdi.
Güler, firmanın incelemelerini tamamlamasının ardından kamuoyunu bilgilendireceklerini sözlerine ekledi.
Bakan Güler, Hürmüz Boğazı'nda enerji sevkiyatı aksadığında veya Kızıldeniz'de ticaret gemileri tehdit altında kaldığında, bunun sonuçlarını Türkiye'nin de hissettiğini söyledi.
Özellikle Orta Doğu ve çevresindeki krizlerin Türkiye'ye etkilerini yönetebilmek için Suudi Arabistan ve Pakistan'la mevcut savunma işbirliğine kalıcı ve kurumsal bir zemine oturtmak için anlaşmayı (Mekke Anlaşması) imzaladıklarını ifade eden Güler, anlaşmanın hiçbir ülkeyi hedef almayan savunma amaçlı bir işbirliği ittifakı olduğunu vurguladı.
Güler, anlaşma taraflar arasında savunma alanında düzenli istişare ve koordinasyonu geliştirmeyi, karşılıklı desteğe dayalı güvenlik ihtiyaçlarına cevap vermeyi amaçlayan bir çerçeve sunduğunu ifade etti.
"Öngörülen bu karşılıklı destek, muharip kuvvetlerin herhangi bir tehdit karşısında doğrudan veya ivedi biçimde konuşlandırılması anlamına kesinlikle gelmemektedir. Esas olan şu ki saldırıya uğrayan tarafın ihtiyaç duyduğu desteğin niteliğini belirleyerek talepte bulunması öngörülmektedir. Buna göre sağlanabilecek desteğin türü ve kapsamı, tehdidin ölçeği, niteliği, ilgili ülkenin ihtiyaçları ve tarafların milli değerlendirmeleri doğrultusunda ele alınacaktır. Ayrıca NATO üyeliğimizden doğan hak ve yükümlülüklerimiz de anlaşmanın 12. maddesiyle saklı tutulmaktadır."
Bu işbirliğinde temel ölçünün Türkiye'nin güvenlik ihtiyacı olduğuna işaret eden Güler, şöyle devam etti.
"Binlerce yıllık kadim devlet aklının önemli bir yansıması olan Türk Silahlı Kuvvetlerimiz, köklü tarihinden daima ilham ve ibret almaktadır. Bu anlayışla ortak çıkarımızın bulunduğu alanlarda hazırlığımızı önceden yapıyoruz. Bir kriz çıktığında ise olayın anlaşma kapsamına girip girmediğini ve Türkiye'nin hangi katkıyı sunacağını somut şartlara göre değerlendiriyoruz. Sonuç olarak Türkiye'nin hangi sorumluluğu hangi şartlarda üstleneceğine Türkiye kendi anayasal…
texts.https://www.wired.com/story/voyager-1-be:
One of NASA’s longest-tenured spacecraft is quite literally stuck in the past.
Voyager 1 , launched in September 1977 toward the outer planets of our solar system, achieved a historic milestone on Wednesday: It became the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth. The spacecraft is so far away , that by the time its light reaches Earth, it comes from the spacecraft as it existed one day in the past. The achievement is one researchers hadn’t planned on , and yet, as Voyager 1 wades deeper into uncharted stretches of the galaxy, it continues sending back valuable scientific information.
“It's just a wonderful happenstance,” Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, says of the milestone. “Just as the stars were aligned for the tour of the planets, they're also aligned for this really magical, special thing that's happening for humankind.”
For Fran Bagenal, a planetary scientist at the University of Colorado, Boulder, who began working with Voyager 1 as a graduate student during its earliest years, the occasion is a momentous technological feat. “What's exciting is the fact that we have a spacecraft that was built in the mid ’70s that is still working,” she says. “Storing data on an eight-track tape that’s working on a spacecraft after 50 years—I mean, it’s amazing.”
Even as Voyager 1 approaches its 50-year anniversary next September, and its end of mission perhaps not long after that, the spacecraft is still checking items off its laundry list of scientific achievements. The spacecraft—alongside its twin, Voyager 2—was originally intended to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment to observe the outer planets .
But Voyager 1 kept traveling beyond the solar system and is now exploring the interstellar medium that fills the space between star systems. Voyager 1’s remoteness gives researchers a rare opportunity to study how the effects of the sun ripple even into the interstellar medium—and at what point those effects wane, says Jamie Rankin, deputy project scientist for the Voyager Mission at Princeton University.
Just as both Voyager spacecraft are moving through space, so is our own solar system—only about 35,000 miles per hour slower, Badaruddin says. That means that as the pair continue their journeys, they’re sending back information about the space that our own sun and planet will pass through in about three years’ time.
“We can learn from telescopes and Earth-orbiting observatories, but there's really nothing like having a spacecraft in that environment that's sending us data,” Badaruddin says.
Voyager 1’s unprecedented journey isn’t without challenges. The craft has stayed in communication with Earth far longer than planned and is trekking through regions of space that it was never built to encounter or study. Researchers are helping maintain crucial functions, but they’re now doing so with a full day of lag in communications both to and from the spacecraft, Badaruddin says.
“Light time is really affecting us,” he says. “You factor it in. It’s like having a long commute.” Building new commands for the spacecraft is now a week-long process, for instance, since it takes time to receive data from the spacecraft, analyze it, and create a new command, he adds.
Still, the Voyager team is used to navigating unforeseen circumstances. For decades, they’ve been managing to make do with a dwindling power supply coming from the craft’s nuclear generators. In September, mission operations switched off some of Voyager 1’s devices in lieu of lower-power alternatives, a maneuver the team dubbed the “Big Bang.” The swap, which saved the craft 10 watts of power, kept mission operations from having to switch off another instrument as early as next summer.
Even when contact with Voyager 1 is eventually lost, the spacecraft will leave a lasting legacy—especially for any future such far-traveling missions, should NASA or another space agency launch one. A successor to Voyager might, for instance, have new devices such as a dust instrument to better analyze the interstellar medium or cameras to give astronomers a better view of these distant stretches of the cosmos, Rankin says.
“I would hope that the Voyagers and their reaching interstellar space has taught us the lesson that we've got to just keep reaching for the stars,” she adds.
Every mission must meet its end, though. And Badaruddin’s best guess is that Voyager 1’s could come in the next three to five years, as the plutonium-238 powering it decays further. Once the craft transmits its final signal to Earth, it will still continue its silent tour of the galaxy.
But Badaruddin acknowledges he’s part of a lineage of mission managers who have said that the spacecraft only has a few years left, only to be proven wrong . “The Big Bang was a rabbit we pulled out of a hat. As long as we can keep finding rabbits, we can keep going,” he says. “Don’t bet against Voyager.”

GTA 6 için milyonlarca kişi oyun konsollarının başında bekliyor. Peki Grand Theft Auto (GTA) video oyunu neden nesiller boyunca bu kadar büyük bir heyecan yaratıyor?
GTA 6 adlı video oyununun piyasaya çıkışına birkaç gün kala yayımlanan son fragmanı böyleydi.
Meraklıları oyunu haftalar öncesinden bilgisayarlarına indirdi. Ve nihayet o gün geldi ve Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6 kullanıma 19 Kasım'dan itibaren açılıyor.
Oyun konsollarının başına geçen milyonlarca kişi şimdi kriminal çift Jason ve Lucia ile birlikte, şık bir spor arabayla kurgusal ABD metropolü Vice City'de gaza basacak. Oyunun boyutu nedeniyle indirme işlemi, internet bağlantısına bağlı olarak günler sürebiliyor. İnternet sağlayıcıları son günlerde veri trafiğinde belirgin bir artış tespit etti.
Yıllardır eşi benzeri görülmemiş bir heyecanla beklenen GTA 6, şimdiden rekorlar kırıyor. Bugüne kadar hiçbir oyun bu kadar fazla ön sipariş verilmedi. Tahminlere göre yaklaşık on milyon kişi oyunu şimdiden satın aldı. GTA 6, abartısız söylemek gerekirse, küresel çapta bir kültür fenomeni hâline gelmiş durumda.
Oyunda GTA 6'nın kurgusal dünyasının esinlendiği Miami, Vice City'ye dönüşüyor. Miami kenti de bu esinlenmeden mutlu. Hatta NBA takımlarından Miami Heat, "Vice City" adı yazılı özel formalarla sahaya çıktı. Oyunun müziklerinde yer alan sanatçılar Miami'de düzenlenen festivallerde sahne alıyor. Pazarlama kampanyasının bir parçası olan "Vice City" tabelası da yol kenarlarına monte bile edildi.
Oyundan beklentiler büyük. Yaklaşık 5 bin kişi on yılı aşkın bir süre boyunca oyun üzerinde çalıştı. Geliştirme maliyetinin 1,5 milyar ABD dolarından fazla olduğu tahmin ediliyor.
Neu-Ulm Üniversitesi'nde kültür bilimci ve oyun tasarımı ile oyun çalışmaları profesörü olan Rudolf Thomas Inderst, "Yalnızca bu rakamlar nedeniyle ve elbette serinin son derece başarılı ve popüler geçmişi sayesinde, en azından çok büyük bir istisnai çıkıştan söz edebiliriz" diyor. Inderst'e göre, çok fazla emek harcanmış bir üründen insanların çok büyük beklentiler içinde olması son derece doğal. GTA 6, günümüzde oyunların oynanış, anlatım, görsellik ve teknik açıdan nelere kadir olduğunu gösterecek.
Video oyunu serisi neredeyse 30 yıldır var ve çıtayı sürekli olarak yükseltti. GTA, siyaset, kültür ve medyayı parodi konusu yapıyor, ABD toplumuna ve "Amerikan Rüyası'na" yönelik acımasız bir hiciv sunuyor. Seri ayrıca oyun özgürlüğünü temsil ediyor.
Oyuncular bu dünyada diledikleri her şeyi yapabiliyor: Bir helikopteri roketatarla düşürmek, berbere gitmek, sahilde yürüyüş yapmak, gece kulüplerini ziyaret etmek, araba yarışlarına katılmak ve daha fazlası.
Oyunla ilgili sıra dışı olan noktalardan biri de kurgusal dünyadaki tüm karakterlerin canlı görünmesi. GTA 6'da bu karakterler oyuncuların davranışlarına şahsına münhasır bir tepki veriyor. Kişiliklerine bağlı olarak örneğin daha korkak ya da daha saldırgan davranıyorlar. Oyunda yaklaşık 600 bin kişi animasyonu var.
GTA 6'nın dünyası yetişkinler için devasa bir oyun parkı. Y kuşağı GTA 3, GTA: Vice City, GTA: San Andreas ve GTA 4 ile büyüdü, Z kuşağı ise GTA 5 ile. Alfa kuşağı aslında GTA 6 için henüz çok genç ancak büyük olasılıkla oyunu yine de oynamanın bir yolunu bulacaklar.
Serinin özellikle GTA 5'in ve çok oyunculu türevi GTA Online'ın kalıcı başarısında, sosyal medyanın da kuşkusuz payı var. Çok sayıda içerik üreticisi oyun oturumlarını Twitch ya da YouTube'da yayınlıyor, özellikle komik oyun sahneleri TikTok'ta paylaşılıyor.
Öte yandan bazı oyuncular GTA dünyasında buluşuyor ve tutarlı biçimde kendilerine belirledikleri canlandırıyor. Örneğin taksi şoförü, yargıç ya da işsiz küçük çaplı suçlu rolüne bürünüyor ve karakterleri için inandırıcı arka plan hikâyeleri uyduruyorlar. Kimileri bunun için bir aksan bile ediniyor.
GTA 6'ya yönelik heyecan yalnızca oyunun kendisine fayda sağlamakla kalmayabilir, daha fazla insanı yeniden konsolların başına çekerek tüm oyun sektörüne de ivme kazandırabilir. Zira Covid-19 salgını sırasında yaşanan yükselişi, stüdyo kapanışları ve işten çıkarmalar izledi. Tahminlere göre, 2022'den bu yana dünya genelinde oyun sektöründen 50 binden fazla kişi işini kaybetti.
Ancak GTA'yı geliştiren stüdyo Rockstar'ın görkemli ürünleri ne kadar ayrıntıya düşkün olsa da hayranların takdir ettiği bu mükemmeliyetçiliğin gölge tarafları da var. Rockstar şirketi, diğer birçok oyun firması gibi, uzun yıllardır çalışma koşulları nedeniyle eleştiri konusu oluyor.
Kültür bilimci Rudolf Thomas Inderst, "Çalışanların içsel motivasyonunun bu kadar güçlü olduğu her yerde, sömürüye başvurmak da cazip hale geliyor" diyor.
Eski geliştiriciler aşırı çalışma saatlerini ve artık sağlıklı olmayan yüksek iş yükünü anlatıyor. Sendikacılar, yönetimin kendilerini gözetim altında tuttuğunu ve çalışmalarını sabote ettiğini öne sürüyor.
Oyunu geliştirenlere şimdi bir sendikanın tanınması için mücadele veriyor. Bu sendika, onlara çalışma saatleri, maaşlar, emeklilik planı ve ebeveyn izni düzenlemeleri gibi konularda söz sahibi olma imkânı sağlayacak. Başarılı olurlarsa bu, adil çalışma koşullarını sağlamakta çoğu zaman hâlâ zorlanan oyun sektörü için güçlü bir sinyal olacak.

Black Friday is still over a week away, but you can already save on Apple devices, chargers, robovacs, and more.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
The countdown to Black Friday is on, and the discounts are starting to appear. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a host of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected next week.
Below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to update this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.
Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review .
Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.
007 First Light , a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman , is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.
Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.
The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review .
Philips Hue bulbs can be pricey, which is why the company’s four-pack of Essential A19 bulbs is a great buy at the current sale price. The adjustable bulbs offer white and color ambiance, 800 lumens of brightness, and can be controlled either via Bluetooth or a Hue Bridge (sold separately).
Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.
You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review .
Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review .
The cheaper, more streamlined SoundLink Max features a slightly smaller battery (16 vs. 20 hours) and lacks external power bank functionality. Otherwise, it’s the same as the standard model, which means the audio is just as great.
Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.
Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.
JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.
Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.
The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.
Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.
Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.
Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.
Tessan’s universal travel adapter delivers up to 205W of combined USB charging power and can charge up to eight devices, including a pair of laptops, at the same time. It features six USB-C ports, including two that can deliver up to 140W individually, a USB-A port, and an AC outlet. It also works in over 200 countries and regions.
Bambu Lab’s P2S Combo is a 3D printer that can print in multiple colors and automatically dry its materials to help improve print quality. It also features a 5-inch touchscreen, a built-in camera for monitoring prints remotely, and AI-powered tools that can detect printing problems.
Eight Sleep’s Pod 6 automatically adjusts your bed’s temperature based on your sleep patterns, heart rate, and breathing. It features a redesigned hub that’s half the size of its predecessor and adjusts temperatures faster. The system also tracks sleep quality, detects snoring, and lets couples control the temperature on each side of the bed independently.
Flextail’s Zero Pump 2 might weigh a mere 1.7 ounces, but it can quickly inflate and deflate a sleeping pad. It comes with six nozzles and a replaceable battery that recharges via USB-C, allowing you to inflate up to 30 pads on a single charge.
The last-gen Litter-Robot 4 can monitor your cat’s visits, track their weight, and automatically separate waste from clean litter after each use, so you can go up to eight days without emptying your cat’s litter box. The so-called starter bundle also includes 20 pounds of litter, 25 waste drawer liners, a host of odor-control accessories, a litter-trapping mat, and a three-year warranty.

texts.https://www.theverge.com/games/1036140/w:
MyMems, from the creator of SimCity and The Sims, is a new social simulator powered by AI.
Will Wright, the creator of legendary franchises like SimCity and The Sims , is working on a new game — and it’s built around AI. The new title, focused on your memories, is called MyMems . Like Wright’s other titles, it sounds extremely ambitious, giving players a new way to explore worlds they create on their own. “We want to take your autobiography and turn it into a toy world,” he tells The Verge .
The MyMems website describes the mobile game as a “social simulation” with worlds “built from your memories and the people who shaped you.” You can add “memories” to your game, like speaking a short story to your phone, and those memories are generated into pieces you can place on the game’s map. Your worlds can also include AI-powered avatars, which can represent people you know in your life. Ideally, as you play, the planet starts to become a “map of your psyche,” kind of like Inside Out , Wright says. Worlds can be private, but you can also share them with others.
Here’s another way to think of it, from Virginia McArthur, executive producer and GM at MyMems developer Gallium Studios: “It’s a cozy world builder with a really deep social simulation underneath.”
I’ll admit that I don’t totally get it, and it seems like a tricky idea to grasp without playing it. Still, as heady of a concept as it might be — turning your memories into a game world — Wright and team still want it to be fun. “This isn’t meant to be your legacy diary necessarily,” says Anthony Maitz, a product manager at Gallium Studios. “It’s meant to just be something you kind of play around with.” However, Maitz notes that what you’re working toward is a “proxy” of you — a word that seems to be the inspiration of the game’s earlier title, Proxi: Yesterday’s You Tomorrow . The game will use the “Behavior Engine” from a company called Artificial Agency , which makes AI tech for video games, as a “foundational technology.”
Like other industries, gaming is starting to reckon with generative AI. Early AI virtual worlds created with models from a startup backed by a Pixar cofounder and Google’s Project Genie weren’t experiences you’d actually want to spend dedicated time with, and indie developers I spoke to in March were largely opposed to the technology . But AI technology has taken some big leaps this year with companies like Google , Meta , and Roblox now letting users make games with AI right from their phone, and retro gaming becoming overrun with AI-powered ports of classic titles.
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said earlier this year that generative AI has “zero part in what Rockstar Games is building” with GTA VI . But even as a recent industry survey indicated that more game developers are starting to use generative AI as part of their job , workers are pushing back against generative AI use , and the technology is at the center of fierce debates over indie game awards .
Many players are rejecting AI outright, and I wondered if the Gallium Studios team was worried about opposition toward MyMems ’ use of AI. Wright says he has three boys at home and that they are all “pretty negative” on AI. He attributes negativity over AI to be toward the meaning of art and authorship and credit, a concern he calls “well-founded.” But he also calls AI an “amazing tool.”
“We’re not making slop,” says McArthur. But Maitz notes that while the team has “been concerned” about a negative response to the generative AI use, they’ve learned that people don’t mind when they use AI in a “ Scribblenauts -y style” for things like having the game make a high school. The team also found that people got “addicted” to a test app with a character creator, including Maitz’s own daughter, who he says “hates” AI. “By making it so that the player is authoring it over and over, bit by bit, it doesn’t really feel like you cheated,” Maitz says.
MyMems , which is set to launch in 2027, will join a growing field of other social simulations, like Krafton’s Inzoi and Nintendo’s smash hit Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream . But none quite have the pull of The Sims , which remains one of EA’s most important franchises. With The Sims , Wright says that many people tried making their real families in the game.
“It was interesting how people really were naturally trying to map this game, which was like a little toy, onto their real life,” he says. With MyMems , that’s what the team is trying to do the “follow-through” on — what if they made the whole game focused on you?
Imagine opening a family scrapbook and the way people and things jump out, Wright explains. “As you go through more and more pages, pretty soon you have this whole little circus of people and events and things from your life.” It’s chaos, he says. “I want something that feels kind of like that.”

With MyMems , Wright says he wants to “turn the simulation inward.”
The computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity , The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA . Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players’ memories.
MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turn[ing] the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world.
“If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?” Wright says by way of example in the release. “If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?”
In an accompanying announcement video , Wright talks about how the “plausible behavior” in a game like The Sims still didn’t effectively capture the nuances of people he encounters in real life. “It was nowhere near them understanding my claustrophobia or why my sister and I fought so much… We’re actually taking parts of your life, your memories, your experiences, people you know, and turning that into a game that’s very personal.”
Wright said MyMems will be able to extract generalized themes from your memories into self-contained areas that Wright compared to the various parts in a theme park: Sports, vacations, injuries, memories, and deaths could all be the basis for their own zones to play in. Players will also have the option to create worlds based on shared memories with family, friends, and co-workers, for example.
Since this is 2026, it shouldn’t be surprising that MyMems is making heavy use of generative AI (with a “proprietary behavior engine” on top) to transform your typed-up memories into simulated locales and characters. In the announcement video, Wright praises the “entirely open-ended” AI systems Gallium is using “to extract from the stories and whatnot based upon the memories you put into the game.”
But Wright’s focus on mining memories for simulation content predates the current generative AI boom. What has now become MyMems started off as Proxi , a mobile simulation that was first announced in 2018 as “a game of self-discovery, a game where we actually uncover the hidden you.” But after years of pre-production work (as outlined in an excellent Vulture piece earlier this year ), Wright’s Gallium Studios finally ran out of funding in late 2024, leading to mass layoffs for the small team and an uncertain future for the project.
Now the idea has been revived thanks in large part to a partnership with AI middleware firm Artificial Agency . Until now, that company has mainly been focused on agentic systems that can create “virtual players” to playtest a game or serve as a partner for human players.
Now, Artificial Agency’s marketing says the company’s AI tool will be used to create “a personal behavior model and a knowledge graph” from players’ memories, drawing some unsettling comparisons to big tech surveillance.
“Meta knows what you click,” the company writes. “Netflix knows what you watch. Nobody knows what you remember. MemDNA learns from your memories locally and only with your permission.”
Wright said the partnership with Artificial Agency will let Gallium benefit from “off-the-shelf” AI solutions without having to “become an AI research company” in its own right. He also said the collaboration will help limit costs by providing a cheaper option than the “really expensive” frontier models that might be overkill for a project like this.
“Right now AI has opened a vast new design area and I’m enjoying, you know, exploring that as a designer,” Wright said.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took time during a high-level diplomatic summit in Asia on Wednesday to try and soothe public US jitters over a spate of cyber-related disruptions.
Rubio insisted authorities have found "zero evidence" that recent outages across tech platforms are related to one another or due to the work of "nefarious actors."
His comments, on the sidelines of a Southeast Asia summit, follow multiple disruptions of everything from US air traffic operations to Microsoft email and messaging to banking and mobile pay, as well as the outage of a top-secret US government communications network.
"The first thing I want to make very clear is that we have zero evidence whatsoever, we have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other," Rubio told reporters in Manila while on a trip to Asia with US President Donald Trump.
"The second is that we have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind."
Rubio emphasised the ubiquity of technology when explaining why it could feel as if there was a growing wave of cyber incidents.
"The more technology becomes embedded into our everyday lives, the more the vulnerabilities become real," he said.
"There was a time when people used to physically go in with masks and guns and rob banks. Now they can do it from behind a computer screen halfway around the world and every major economy in the world is facing that same challenge."
On Tuesday a top-secret network that the National Security Agency (NSA) uses for internal communications went down, the agency acknowledged.
The NSA said it had experienced "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," but that its capabilities remained operational and "our ability to defend national security continues."
The NSA, part of the US Department of Defence, is responsible for global monitoring, collection and processing of information for intelligence and counterintelligence.
The Trump administration has insisted Americans and their various systems remain secure, with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin emphasizing that the wave of recent outages does not stem from cyber criminals.
"I can tell you with complete certainty that we are not under attack," Mullin told CNBC. "There's no cyber threat that's taking place. The homeland is very secure."
Air travel was disrupted because of what the Trump administration called outdated equipment, causing regulators to halt all flights from taking off for several hours on Friday evening.
The mess of stranded travellers and aircrews spilled into the weekend and early this week.
Microsoft also suffered a major outage last week that affected Outlook and Teams users around the world, while several large banks saw disruptions to their banking apps and online portals on Monday.
Trump's rival Democratic Party, which just won decisively in US midterm elections earlier this month, blamed the administration's incompetence for the string of high-visibility outages and the lack of transparency around them.
"We've had the Microsoft incident, then we had the nationwide ground stop. Now we have concerns as it relates to highly classified servers over at the NSA," Hakeem Jeffries, a top Democrat in Congress, told reporters.
"I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves, so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people of the United States of America."

Şirketin geçici Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Colette Kress, daha önce ABD yönetiminin ihracat izni verdiği Hopper serisi veri merkezi işlemcilerinin artık Çin'e gönderilmediğini bildirdi. Söz konusu karar, Nvidia'nın Çin pazarındaki geleceğine ilişkin soru işaretlerini artırırken ABD ile Çin arasındaki yarı iletken rekabetini de yeniden gündeme taşıdı.
Nvidia'nın açıklaması, şirketin 17 Kasım'da gerçekleştirdiği mali sonuç toplantısında geldi. Kress, 25 Ekim'de sona eren çeyrekte Çin'e lisans kapsamında 2,4 milyar dolar değerinde Hopper serisi ürün satıldığını, ancak gelecek döneme ilişkin sevkiyat beklentilerinde Çin'e yönelik bu ürünlere yer verilmediğini söyledi.
Kress, şirketin artık Çin'e lisanslı Hopper veri merkezi ürünleri göndermediğini belirtirken kararın gerekçesine veya sevkiyatların ne zaman yeniden başlayabileceğine ilişkin ayrıntı paylaşmadı. Dolayısıyla Nvidia'nın bu adımının kalıcı bir satış yasağı mı yoksa mevcut koşullara bağlı bir sevkiyat durdurma kararı mı olduğu henüz bilinmiyor.
Nvidia'nın açıklaması, Çin'e yönelik bütün ürün satışlarının sona erdiği anlamına gelmiyor. Karar, özellikle Hopper ailesindeki veri merkezi ürünlerini kapsıyor. Bu ailenin en önemli işlemcilerinden biri olan H200, yapay zeka modellerinin eğitilmesi ve çalıştırılmasında kullanılıyor. Şirketin daha düşük kapasiteli ve ihracat kurallarına uygun bazı ürünleri içinse farklı bir tablo söz konusu.
Nvidia'nın son kararı, tek başına alınmış bir şirket kararından çok daha büyük bir mücadelenin parçası. ABD'nin Çin'in gelişmiş yarı iletkenlere erişimini sınırlandırması, Pekin'in yabancı teknolojiye bağımlılığı azaltma politikası ve iki ülkenin yapay zeka alanında üstünlük kurma çabası, bugünkü tablonun oluşmasında etkili oldu.
Üstelik Washington ve Pekin'in Nvidia çiplerine yönelik politikaları her zaman aynı yönde ilerlemedi. ABD bazı işlemcilerin ihracatına izin verirken Çin yönetimi aynı ürünlerin ülkeye girişini sınırlandırdı. Bu durum, Nvidia'yı iki farklı düzenleyici sistemin arasında bıraktı.
ABD, Çin'in gelişmiş yarı iletkenlere ve bu çipleri üretmek için kullanılan teknolojilere erişimini sınırlandırmak amacıyla Ekim 2022'de kapsamlı ihracat kontrolleri uygulamaya başladı. Washington yönetiminin temel gerekçesi, gelişmiş işlem gücünün Çin ordusu tarafından kullanılabilecek yapay zeka sistemlerinin geliştirilmesini kolaylaştırmasıydı.
Kısıtlamalar, Nvidia'nın A100 ve H100 gibi yüksek performanslı veri merkezi işlemcilerini de etkiledi. Şirket, Çin pazarındaki faaliyetlerini sürdürebilmek için ABD'nin belirlediği teknik eşiklere uygun, performansı sınırlandırılmış ürünler geliştirmek zorunda kaldı.
Washington, Ekim 2023'te kuralları güncelleyerek yalnızca işlem gücünü değil, çiplerin bellek bant genişliği ve işlem yoğunluğu gibi teknik özelliklerini de kapsayan yeni sınırlamalar getirdi. Böylece şirketlerin mevcut kuralları aşmak için daha düşük performanslı işlemciler tasarlaması da zorlaştı.
Nvidia'nın Çin pazarı için geliştirdiği H20 işlemcisi, ABD'nin ihracat kurallarına uyum sağlamak amacıyla performansı sınırlandırılmış ürünlerden biriydi. Ancak ABD yönetimi Nisan 2025'te bu işlemcinin Çin'e ihracatı için de lisans zorunluluğu getirdi.
Kararın ardından Nvidia, satılamayan H20 ürünleri ve üretim taahhütleri nedeniyle 2026 mali yılının ilk çeyreğinde 4,5 milyar dolarlık gider kaydetti. ABD yönetimi Ağustos 2025'te bazı Çinli müşterilere H20 gönderilmesine izin veren lisanslar verse de bu kez Çin yönetiminin kısıtlamaları devreye girdi. Nvidia'nın mali raporlarına göre şirket, Çin'in kendi sınırlandırmaları nedeniyle bu ürünlerin tamamını satamadı.
Bu gelişme, Nvidia'nın Çin pazarında karşılaştığı sorunun yalnızca ABD'nin ihracat politikalarıyla sınırlı olmadığını gösterdi. Şirket bir taraftan Washington'ın belirlediği teknik sınırları aşmadan ürün geliştirmeye çalışırken diğer taraftan Pekin'in yerli çip üreticilerini destekleyen politikalarıyla karşı karşıya kaldı.
ABD ile Çin arasındaki gerilime rağmen Donald Trump yönetimi, Aralık 2025'te Nvidia'nın H200 işlemcilerinin belirli Çinli müşterilere satılmasına izin verileceğini duyurdu. Bu karar, Nvidia'nın Çin pazarına yeniden erişebilmesi açısından önemli bir gelişmeydi.
ABD Ticaret Bakanlığına bağlı Sanayi ve Güvenlik Bürosu (BIS), 13 Ocak 2026'da ihracat lisanslarının değerlendirilmesine ilişkin politikasını değiştirdi. Daha önce reddedilme ihtimali esas alınarak değerlendirilen bazı gelişmiş işlemciler için artık belirli güvenlik koşullarının sağlanması durumunda başvuru bazında inceleme yapılabilecekti.
Bu düzenleme yalnızca Nvidia H200 işlemcisini değil, AMD'nin MI325X modeli gibi benzer özelliklere sahip ürünleri de kapsıyordu.
İzin, koşulsuz bir satış serbestisi anlamına gelmiyordu. ABD yönetiminin belirlediği şartlar arasında Çin'e gönderilecek ürünlerin ABD'deki müşterilere ayrılan küresel üretim kapasitesini azaltmaması, Çinli alıcıların ihracat kurallarına uyum ve müşteri denetimi için yeterli güvenlik prosedürlerine sahip olması, çiplerin sevkiyat öncesinde ABD'de bağımsız bir kuruluş tarafından teknik ve güvenlik testlerinden geçirilmesi ve ihracatın belirlenen performans ve güvenlik sınırları içinde kalması bulunuyordu.
H200 satışları için getirilen bir diğer dikkat çekici koşul ise yüzde 25'lik gümrük tarifesiydi. Çiplerin Çin'e gönderilmeden önce ABD'ye ithal edilmesi ve gerekli denetimlerden geçirilmesi öngörülüyordu. Bu süreç, satışın maliyetini ve lojistik koşullarını da değiştirdi.
Böylece ABD, Nvidia'nın Çin'e tamamen sırtını dönmesini istemeyen ticari yaklaşımı ile gelişmiş işlem gücünün Çin'in askerî ve stratejik kapasitesini artırabileceği yönündeki güvenlik kaygılarını aynı politikada buluşturmaya çalıştı. Ancak bu kez de Pekin'in onayı ve yerli üreticileri önceleyen politikası, planlanan satışların önünde engel oluşturdu.
ABD'nin H200 satışlarına izin vermesi, Çinli teknoloji şirketlerinin bu işlemcilere kolayca erişebileceği anlamına gelmedi. Çin yönetimi, Nvidia'nın gelişmiş işlemcilerine yönelik ithalatı sınırlandırarak yerli yarı iletken üreticilerini desteklemeye yönelik politikasını sürdürdü.

In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump’s pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation.
Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy’s decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats.
In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA’s current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn’t say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is “quite lethal” or that children are given vaccine doses the “size of a soda bottle.” Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong.
Axios quoted a senior Trump administration official as saying that Overton’s nomination was dropped because she “lacks the support on the Hill to move forward with her confirmation.”
The Senate’s Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, chaired by Bill Cassidy (R-La.), was scheduled to vote on Overton’s nomination Wednesday. In a social media post Tuesday night, after her nomination was withdrawn, Cassidy said he believed she had a “viable confirmation path.” But he said the nomination was “abandoned” after some anti-abortion senators sought commitments from her that they couldn’t get. “The Administration withdrew Dr. Overton rather than make such commitments,” Cassidy said.
“Unfortunately, with the limited time left, confirming a permanent FDA Commissioner will fall to Senate Democrats,” Cassidy noted.
After Overton’s last-minute withdrawal, the HELP committee’s agenda for Wednesday was updated again this morning to scrap a scheduled vote on Jim O’Neill, who was Trump’s nominee to run the NSF.
O’Neill has been criticized for lacking the science experience needed to run the foundation. In the past, O’Neill worked as a Silicon Valley investor and entrepreneur and became a close ally of Peter Thiel. But under Trump, O’Neill has been the deputy secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services and served as acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. O’Neill took over the latter role after the former director, Susan Monarez, was ousted from it less than a month after her Senate confirmation. She later told Senators Kennedy fired her for refusing to blindly approve vaccine recommendations from his anti-vaccine advisors.
In remarks this morning , Cassidy said that O’Neill “did not do enough to stand up for science and against irresponsible decisions and statements from [Health] Secretary [Robert F.] Kennedy [Jr.].” As an example, Cassidy specifically referenced O’Neill’s role in the firing of Monarez. “Several members of the [HELP] committee had concerns regarding this,” Cassidy said.
“This time requires leadership and fortitude and standing up for what is right,” Cassidy added.
The NSF has been hard hit by the Trump administration and actions by Elon Musk’s DOGE. The NSF has been forced to cancel hundreds of research grants and taken brutal cuts to its budget and staff in the past two years. In April, the Trump administration also terminated all members of the board that steers the NSF, called the National Science Board. Former members feared that it would make way for O’Neill to stack the board with political allies, pointing to how Trump filled the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology with tech billionaires —including leaders of Meta, Google, Oracle, and Nvidia—instead of top scientists and researchers.

Trump is stacking the FCC with Republicans, even as the Democrats boycott.
Senate commerce committee Chair Ted Cruz (R-TX) began a meeting Wednesday meant to confirm President Donald Trump’s nominee to the Federal Communications Commission with a lopsided dais. To his right sat all 14 Republican members of the panel, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD). To his left were about a dozen empty chairs — every Democratic member of the panel was absent.
Cruz said he’d learned the night before that Democrats intended to boycott the vote, though Democrats say they’d repeatedly raised their concerns about advancing a Republican FCC nominee without a Democratic one. “The administration has shown it’s willing to move Democrats,” Cruz said, pointing to Senate votes scheduled on bipartisan pairs of nominations to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission. And even though the Supreme Court confirmed his power to do so, Cruz said, Trump has not moved to fire any Democrats from the FCC , as he did at the Federal Trade Commission . “This is an ordinary nomination to fill a vacancy previously held by someone in the same party,” Cruz said.
“This is an ordinary nomination to fill a vacancy previously held by someone in the same party”
But in statements and comments to reporters outside the committee room, Democrats said that the process has been far from normal. Senate committees often vote on nominations to historically independent agencies in bipartisan pairs. Confirming Danielle Thumann Severs, senior counsel to FCC Chair Brendan Carr, to become a commissioner at the agency would put the FCC at four total members — three Republicans and one Democrat, Anna Gomez. Gomez’s term has technically expired, though she can remain on the commission through next year unless she’s replaced. But Democrats fear that by confirming a third Republican to the FCC, Trump might finally fire Gomez , because he’d no longer need her present for a quorum to vote on key actions.
Democrats asked for Thumann’s confirmation vote to be withheld until her nomination could be paired with a Democratic nomination. One way to do that would be to renominate Gomez. But so far, the president has not offered any Democratic nominees for the commission. Democrats said they made their concerns clear to Cruz, and added, “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In addition to the procedural concerns, Democrats worry about Thumann’s work as an adviser to Carr, and whether she was truthful about the matters she worked on. In a letter asking Cruz to delay her confirmation vote, Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-NM) detailed his concerns. At the November 10th hearing where Thumann answered committee members’ questions, she testified that she had “not worked with the Chairman on any media-related issues,” Luján noted in the letter. But documents obtained via a Freedom of Information Act request show that Thumann was “looped in” on various media matters, and “helped draft Skydance’s commitments that facilitated the 2 FCC’s approval of the Skydance-Paramount merger,” Luján wrote. “She also played a role in processing informal complaints related to CBS 60 Minutes alleged news distortion and she apparently orchestrated the Commission’s response to consumers regarding the Jimmy Kimmel controversy.” The FCC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the matter.
Even Cruz admitted concerns with Carr’s handling of Kimmel’s comments in the aftermath of conservative activist Charlie Kirk’s killing. But at Wednesday’s meeting, he said he “emphatically agree[s]” that Thumann had resolved any lingering worries about that. He added that his JAWBONE Act , which the committee previously passed, could directly address First Amendment violations by government agencies of either party. The bill would let individuals sue government officials if they illegally try to compel social media or broadcast companies to remove their speech. Sen. Jerry Moran (R-KS), who’d similarly expressed concern over the Kimmel incident, said he found Thumann’s responses on the subject “comforting,” including in a phone call earlier that morning where he said he’d expressed his “serious interest in how the FCC protects and promotes free speech, including free speech on broadcast.” On the call, he said, “she was able to satisfy me once again in her answers, including an explanation for her role at the FCC and her lack of engagement on this type of issue as the FCC made decisions.”
“If she was lying about this, what else is she lying about and what else is she hiding?”
Speaking to reporters outside of the hearing room ahead of the meeting, Luján accused Thumann of lying to the committee. “The questions that I have is if she was lying about this, what else is she lying about and what else is she hiding?” he said. Luján said he wants both Thumann and Carr to appear before the committee by the end of the year to answer lawmakers’ questions. Asked if he’d support using the committee’s subpoena power or even pursuing impeachment against Carr when Democrats regain power next year, Luján said his vote to confirm Carr as a commissioner under President Joe Biden is among his biggest regrets, and that while he hopes Carr will testify voluntarily, “everything should be on the table here to be able to get answers for the American people.”
When it came time to vote on whether to advance Thumann’s nomination for a final step of a vote on the Senate floor, all 15 Republicans voted “aye.” That gave Thumann enough votes for her nomination to advance to the Senate floor, where it’s expected to pass along party lines once scheduled. Still, the clerk listed off the names of the 13 Democratic committee members whose seats remained empty. There was no response.

Nvidia is going through it. The chipmaker’s iconic leader just resigned due to an international scandal, its stock has taken a hit, and it’s in a precarious position as it tries to maintain its dominance in the AI era.
Following Jensen Huang’s ouster, the company’s interim CEO and still-CFO Colette Kress has been tasked with stabilizing the deck. So far, Kress’s public-facing duties have included running the company’s third-quarter earnings call and hosting an all-hands meeting for Nvidia’s money-hungry workforce . And as part of her calming campaign, Kress has also been deploying a catchphrase that sounds like it was taken straight from the draft files of a summer of ‘24 Democratic campaign strategist: “We’ve got this.”
By WIRED’s count, Kress has publicly used the phrase three times in the past 24 hours, often putting emphasis or a little bit of zhuzh in it:
“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We’ve got this.”
“Our ambition will not change. Our passion to innovate will not change. Our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change. We thank you all for the great quarter that we had. Just remember, we've got this.”
Kress ended Wednesday’s meeting by comparing Nvidia’s employees to “90,000 people packed into the sweatiest, hottest” University of Florida football game, all singing together.
“It is impressive to see them all together, all in harmony singing that song… Do you know what? We’re gonna hear that song, guys. And I believe in all of you that you will help sing it. But Nvidia, we’ve got this.”
Kress’s new catchphrase perhaps isn’t the most inspiring; companies that got this usually don’t have to remind people how much they got this twice in one meeting. It’s a collectivist’s version of “You got this,” a slightly less corny version of “Yes we can,” a saying that may well pose more questions than it answers. (We got…what?)
Nvidia investors, or any investor, might not have fist-pumped and said, “We’ve got this!” during a quick portfolio check these past 10 days. Anyone who has had the slightest hint of knowledge that Nvidia’s chips were finding their way into China is unlikely to be in a “We totally got this” mood at the moment.
Still, some Nvidia employees appear to be inspired by Kress’s mantra. “Damn right we got this,” Aaron Erickson, Nvidia’s head of NemoClaw engineering, posted on X on Wednesday. Vega Shah, who works in portfolio management for Nvidia’s venture capital arm, shared Erickson’s post and echoed the phrase , adding her own rocket ship emoji to the post.
And yesterday, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said the board did not intend to reinstate Huang, despite some calls on social media and within the company to put Huang back in the top spot.

US secretary of state’s comments come as vulnerability in programming language Java highlighted
There is “zero evidence” that a wave of IT outages – which have grounded flights, cut off work access, limited bank access, affected Apple and disrupted classified communications – are related to each other or are the work of malign actors, according to the US secretary of state.
Marco Rubio said the US was “not under systemic attack” and a cascade of network problems was “not inter-related”.
In recent days, Microsoft , major US banks , Apple , American air traffic control systems and the National Security Agency have all been affected by technical failures and outages.
“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber-hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” Rubio said.
Rubio’s comments came as cybersecurity researchers flagged a vulnerability in Java, a programming language used by 90% of companies in the Fortune 500, a ranking of the largest companies in the US. The researchers at US-based Calif used AI to discover the flaw and recently unearthed glitches in PHP, another computer language.
Calif said the Java flaw could allow hackers to remotely execute code, allowing them to place malicious software on a target’s systems.
The US director of national intelligence, Jay Clayton, said the incidents were caused by security upgrades – such as plugging the flaws in PHP – that took longer than planned or encountered unexpected hiccups.
“Everybody recognises it’s time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected,” he told the Fox Business news channel.
Tal Be’ery, a cybersecurity expert, said he did not believe the incidents were linked directly but had a common underlying theme: AI. IT systems were buckling under the pressure of adding AI or tackling flaws uncovered by AI, he said.
“Our IT infrastructure is brittle, and when AI puts massive extra pressure on it, whether through upgrades to accommodate AI or through the rapid patching that AI-driven vulnerability discovery demands,” Be’ery said.
Since April, when the AI startup Anthropic released its Mythos model, which had a startling ability to flag IT flaws, the amount of vulnerabilities found by leading tech companies has soared eightfold – while OpenAI has also released models capable of finding previously unseen flaws. Researchers at Calif used OpenAI technology to discover the Java flaw.
“[Java] is the beating heart of the modern economy,” Calif wrote in a blogpost . “Banking, aviation, telecommunications, nearly every critical sector runs on Java, including national security systems.”
However, Steven Murdoch, a professor of security engineering at University College London, said the flaw did not apply to every Java user and was specific to a library of code – Base64 – that comes bundled with a version of Java.
“It’s significant but it’s not every Java program that is affected,” he said.
In the UK the National Cyber Security Centre urged organisations to keep their systems up to date, while the US and South Korean authorities also urged Java users to install security updates.
Rubio made the comments as he travelled with Donald Trump for key meetings in the Philippines on Wednesday, before flying to the tech hub of Shenzhen in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
Trump was dismissive when asked whether he was concerned about the outages on Tuesday. “It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said in Manila.
The series of outages began on Thursday last week, when Microsoft’s email and other tools went down , affecting millions of workers who rely on them. Microsoft traced the problem to “an earlier network capacity upgrade”.
Flights across the US were grounded the next day in the longest “ground stop” since the September 11 attacks. The US Federal Aviation Administration blamed a router upgrade.
By Monday, banks were in the spotlight, as customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major financial institutions and the money transfer service Zelle after a technical problem at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. Chase said it was caused by “a software bug” and was “not cyber-related”.
The same day, United Airlines said it had resolved an internal system outage that delayed departing flights.
Then on Tuesday, an internal network that the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline after what the agency described as “routine maintenance”. Apple also confirmed problems with its iPhone apps, such as Apple Pay and iCloud, on Tuesday but said it had resolved them.
The Democrat Mark Warner, the vice-chair of the Senate intelligence committee, supported the assessment that the outages were not caused by a “coordinated effort” but by attempts to shore up systems.
“The evidence so far points toward legitimate efforts to secure our systems, not malicious activity.”
Cynthia Kaiser, a former deputy director in the FBI’s cyber division, said it was “plausible” that the race to upgrade systems was fuelled by warnings that specific cyber adversaries were planning attacks.
Kaiser, now an executive at cybersecurity firm Halcyon, said she was more concerned about cyber criminals and scammers trying to “capitalise on the confusion to steal money from organisations and everyday people ”.

Nvidia , Çin pazarına yönelik stratejisinde önemli bir değişikliğe gidiyor. Şirketin geçici CEO'su Colette Kress , Nvidia'nın artık Çin'e lisanslı Hopper mimarili veri merkezi ürünleri göndermediğini açıkladı . Bu kapsamda şirketin H200 yapay zeka çiplerinin Çin'e sevkiyatı da sona ermiş oldu.
Karar, Nvidia'nın kurucu ortağı ve uzun yıllar CEO'luk görevini üstlenen Jensen Huang'ın geçen hafta görevinden ayrılmasının ardından gerçekleştirilen i lk finansal sonuç toplantısında açıklandı. Aynı gün Nvidia, ulusal güvenlik politikaları, ihracat kontrollerine uyum ve küresel ticaret risklerini takip edecek yönetim kurulu seviyesinde yeni bir komite kurduğunu da duyurdu .
Hatırlatmak gerekirse ABD Başkanı Donald Trump , geçtiğimiz yılın aralık ayında Nvidia'nın H200 çiplerini belirli Çinli müşterilere satmasına izin vermişti . Jensen Huang ve Trump yönetimi arasında şekillenen düzenleme kapsamında çiplerin ABD üzerinden gönderilmesi ve ABD hükümetinin satışlardan yüzde 25 oranında pay alması öngörülüyordu. H200, Nvidia'nın önceki nesil Hopper mimarisini temel almasına rağmen özellikle yapay zeka modellerinin eğitimi ve çalıştırılması açısından halen güçlü bir veri merkezi ürünü olarak öne çıkıyor.
Bloomberg'ün paylaştığı bilgilere göre Nvidia, yalnızca 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde Çin'e yaklaşık 2,4 milyar dolarlık Hopper mimarili veri merkezi ürünü sattı. Jensen Huang, ABD'nin gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerinin Çin'e satışını kısıtlayan politikalarına uzun süredir karşı çıkıyordu. Huang, Çin pazarını tamamen yerel üreticilere bırakmanın ABD teknoloji sektörü açısından olumsuz sonuçlar doğurabileceğini savunuyordu. Nvidia'nın yeni yönetimi altında alınan son karar ise şirketin bu yaklaşımından uzaklaşmaya başladığına işaret ediyor.
Nvidia'nın kararı, ABD'nin Çin'in gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine erişimini sınırlamak amacıyla getirdiği yeni düzenlemelerle aynı döneme denk geliyor. ABD Ticaret Bakanlığı'nın açıkladığı yeni kurallar , Çinli şirketlerin yurt dışındaki veri merkezleri üzerinden gelişmiş ABD çiplerinden yararlanmasını da zorlaştırıyor. Düzenleme kapsamında, Çinli şirketlere belirli bir seviyenin üzerinde işlem gücü sağlayan yabancı veri merkezlerine gelişmiş çip gönderilmesi için ABD'den lisans alınması gerekiyor.
Paylaşılan bilgilere göre; yatırım bankası Jefferies, söz konusu ihracat kurallarının gelecek yıl Nvidia'nın veri merkezi gelirlerinde 44 ila 62 milyar dolar arasında kayba yol açabileceğini tahmin ediyor. Colette Kress ise Vera Rubin gibi yeni nesil Nvidia ürünlerine yönelik güçlü talebin bu kaybın şirketin toplam gelirlerine yansımasını engelleyebileceğini belirtiyor.
Yeni düzenlemelerin uzun vadede Singapur, Malezya, Tayland ve Endonezya gibi ülkelerdeki Nvidia müşterilerini de etkilemesi bekleniyor. Çin'den gelen talebin Nvidia'nın toplam gelirlerinin yüzde 20'sine kadarını oluşturabileceği tahmin ediliyor.
Öte yandan Çin yönetiminin, Nvidia'nın kararından önce de H200 çiplerinin ülkeye girişine sıcak bakmadığı belirtiliyor. Çin, özellikle Huawei gibi yerli üreticilerin geliştirdiği yapay zeka çiplerinin kullanımını artırmayı hedefliyor. Buna rağmen ülkedeki büyük yapay zeka şirketleri, Nvidia'nın gelişmiş çiplerini kullanmaya devam etmek istiyor.
Nvidia'nın H200 satışlarını sonlandırması, Jensen Huang'ın ayrılışının ardından şirketin Çin politikasındaki ilk önemli değişikliklerden biri olarak öne çıkıyor. Yeni ihracat kuralları da göz önüne alındığında, Nvidia'nın önümüzdeki dönemde Çin'e bağlı gelirlerini azaltarak farklı pazarlara ve yeni nesil ürünlere daha fazla ağırlık vermesi beklenebilir.

texts.https://www.npr.org/2026/11/18/nx-s1-604:
China's President Xi Jinping, center, stands as President Trump, left, and Russian President Vladimir Putin shake hands before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, Wednesday. Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press via AP hide caption
SHENZHEN, China — President Donald Trump plans to meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in China, in addition to their already scheduled three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, a U.S. official confirmed.
Trump's meeting with Putin would be the first time that the leaders have held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia's war in Ukraine.
Trump has frequently boasted of his rapport with Putin as relations between the United States and Ukraine appear to have cratered recently. Trump rejected new Russia sanctions while Kyiv was undermined by disruptions in satellite support for its drones during the war.
The U.S. official who confirmed the Trump-Putin meeting in China spoke to The Associated Press on the condition of anonymity to share plans that were not yet public.
The exact timing of the meeting on Thursday was unclear. Trump already had public plans for a separate meeting with Xi and a historic trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin.
Trump said he plans to talk with Xi and Putin in their joint meeting about limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 with Russia's invasion. Analysts are not expecting substantive breakthroughs despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting.
Before the trip, Trump's aides told reporters that the war in Ukraine would not be on the agenda. But Trump said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict.
Russian President Vladimir Putin speaks at the APEC CEO summit held ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, southern China's Guangdong province on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Dmitry Azarov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption
"I think it's very close to getting it done," the Republican president said. "We're going to have a good meeting on that."
Trump landed in China on Wednesday seeking to reinforce America's status as the world's leading technology power, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left his administration scrambling to calm the U.S. public.
The issues put the administration on the defensive at a moment when the president wants to project strength and certainty before the meeting with Xi and Putin.
As he began his trip to Asia, Trump initially had been nonchalant about the outages that left people in the U.S. worried about accessing their email, checking their bank accounts or safely flying on an airplane.
"It's fine," Trump said Tuesday from the Philippine capital of Manila, suggesting it was all just a consequence of being a nation that is "big and powerful."
But then the outages involving Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, JPMorgan Chase and the National Security Agency's communications network began to overshadow Trump's visit. They raised the specter that artificial intelligence can disrupt daily life, as new cyber vulnerabilities identified require software to be constantly upgraded to fix flaws or other security holes, known as patching, which is supposed to improve how the technology runs.
At the start of the second day of Trump's trip, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stepped in to reassure Americans on Trump's behalf. Rubio told reporters there was "zero" evidence that the outages were connected or were tied to rival nations, cyber hackers or criminals.
"Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you've identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption," said Rubio, who is also Trump's national security adviser.
President Trump walks with China's President Xi Jinping as he arrives at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen, in southern China's Guangdong Province, Wednesday. Mark Schiefelbein/AP hide caption
Xi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, reciprocating a gesture by the American leader during Xi's state visit to Washington in September.
Trump and Xi greeted each other on Wednesday at the foot of the airplane's stairs in a handshake that became a hug as a group of dancers waved flowers and flags. When Putin arrived earlier in the day, Xi did not greet him at the airport despite their long-standing friendship.
Trump has signaled that he wants to take an improvised approach during his time in Shenzhen, the skyscraper-filled tech hub that is hosting world leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It's a bet that his unscripted brand of diplomacy based on personal relationships can create some kind of legacy to reshape world affairs during his final two years in the White House.
As leaders were introduced on Wednesday night before an APEC group photo, Putin approached Trump. They shook hands and traded greetings.
The White House said Trump was scheduled earlier Wednesday to have separate meetings with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney before the official APEC greeting ceremony. Trump has previously voiced his disapproval of the U.S. trade pact with Canada and Mexico that was negotiated during his first term.
Before he landed in Shenzhen, Trump had lunch in Manila with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at the Malacañang Presidential Palace.
Marcos noted that he had sent fried chicken from the Philippine chain Jollibee to the U.S. delegation for a late-night snack Tuesday and he complimented Trump for "working very hard."
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., left, walks beside U.S. President Donald Trump during a welcome ceremony marking Trump's state visit to the Philippines at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Aaron Favila/AP hide caption
Trump praised the U.S. bond with the Philippines and the interior decoration of the presidential palace.
"Our people share common history, common values, common interests, common architectural tastes," Trump said. "I love what you've done here."
He said after their meeting that the two nations had reached a trade deal on Wednesday, though he had also said last year that an agreement had been reached.
Trump also had a short reunion with Imelda Marcos, the country's former first lady who is the mother of the Philippines' current president. Famed for her lavish shoe collection, Imelda Marcos knew Trump decades ago through the New York City party scene.
The prospect of Trump meeting with two of America's largest geopolitical rivals has been a source of unease because Trump has been less welcoming of historic allies such as Canada and NATO partners in Europe.
His tariffs that were intended to curb China's trade surplus have done little to stop the progress of the world's dominant manufacturer, which for the second straight year will have exported $1 trillion more in goods than what it imported.
Even without the digital outages in the U.S., questions about how to handle AI loom over the summit.
The technology is viewed as key to unlocking faster economic growth, but its rapid development has meant it poses national security risks and could evolve in ways that put AI beyond human control.
Trump's close tech industry ally Jensen Huang was recently removed as the CEO of Nvidia after he admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be an agent of the Chinese government. Beijing has denied that she was a spy, yet the affair raised concerns about how China has been able to access Nvidia computer chips to develop its own AI models that are competing with the U.S.

Hakeem Jeffries is one step closer to making history as the first Black Speaker of the US House of Representatives, after Democrats nominated him for the powerful role despite a small but vocal group of progressive dissenters.
Jeffries, who has served as House minority leader and leader of the House Democratic Caucus since 2023, secured the nod following a closed-door vote. 251 voted for his nomination, compared with 11 against. The move came ahead of a full House vote when the new Congress convenes in January.
Many of those who voted “no” are a group of progressive newcomers, who said in a statement that there is “still work to be done” to ensure their priorities.
Jeffries, who hails from New York, ran unopposed but says he is taking nothing for granted. He faces a restive party eager for a change after voters ousted Republicans in a rebuke of President Donald Trump and his underlings.
Speaking after his nomination was announced, he vowed to "hold the crooks accountable", referring to Democratic plans to reverse Republican policies and investigate controversial moves by the Trump administration.
"We're going to fight to make sure that, in the face of the unprecedented corruption, chaos, and cruelty visited upon the American people, that House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones, because the American people deserve better," Jeffries told reporters.
His fighting talk came after Democrats unveiled plans for wide-ranging investigations into Trump officials and his business interests when they take control of the House in January.
On Wednesday, Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, sent 12 letters warning members of Trump's family and senior administration figures to preserve documents ahead of investigations into alleged corruption, immigration abuses and the handling of files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Since the midterm elections earlier in November, Democrats, both established and newly-elected, say they’ve been flooded with phone calls and social media posts demanding a fresh start.
Last week, protesters heckled Jeffries during a Democratic conference in Denver, Colorado.
Those opposing Jeffries, including some backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, said conversations are ongoing about his potential new role.
“Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they said in a joint statement.
“We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”
He was nominated alongside Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts and Rep. Pete Aguilar of California, who would also be historic firsts, Clark as the first female majority leader and Aguilar as the first Latino to serve as the majority whip. Both also ran unopposed.
The trio will face another vote when the new Congress convenes for the first time on 3 January, 2027.
Jeffries, Clark and Aguilar have risen together, as a team, as the first new generation of leaders of the post-Pelosi era and will likely serve as leaders in the majority for the first time.
When Rep. Nancy Pelosi of California decided to step aside from leadership in 2022 after the party's electoral defeat that handed Republicans the majority, it set the stage for this very era.
Meanwhile, a similar upheaval with Democrats angling for change is happening in the Senate, where Senate leader Chuck Schumer of New York faces a challenge from Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, a Democrat who’s been the senior United States senator for the state since 2017.

Israeli tanks have advanced towards central Gaza as the military launched what it called a “precise operation” against Hamas, raising fresh tensions over a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025.
An AFP journalist reported seeing tanks, driven by the Israeli military, position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp, which is located in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza .
The AFP also heard from a security source in Gaza who said there was "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of the camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday".

Confirming that the operation involved military and Israeli Security Agency personnel, the IDF said, “there is Hamas infrastructure in the area in the central Gaza Strip.”
COGAT, the Israeli defence ministry body responsible for civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories, has warned international aid organisations not to move through the affected areas.

Hamas condemned the operation as a "flagrant violation" of the ceasefire agreement, accusing Israel of failing to honour its commitments.
The Israeli military, meanwhile, said it was responding to apparent violations of the truce by Hamas.
